A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural-MedBench study. Their main text, tables, figures, equation, and Appendices A–G are readable and matchable despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v4 reports original evaluations of 13 VLMs, human performance baselines, and a 100-response error analysis in Table 2 and Section 5.3.

after.justification: v5 reports evaluations of 16 VLMs alongside the retained human baselines and original error analysis.

M1.justification: The benchmark curation, prompting, and hybrid evaluation pipeline remain unchanged. Expanded difficulty-level descriptions and grader-validation details do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 120 cases, 200 tasks, four clinical data sources, and three difficulty levels. The external benchmark comparisons are also retained; expanded task descriptions do not demonstrate new evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-5, Gemini 2.5-Pro, and Lingshu to the existing comparison roster. HuatuoGPT was already evaluated in v4, and Appendix C confirms that the shortened MedGemma label denotes the retained MedGemma-27B-it model.

E3.justification: The added models use the retained zero-shot evaluation design, prompts, metrics, and decoding settings. Human evaluation remains five students and five senior physicians completing 200 tasks. Newly specified normalization and grader-validation details document existing procedures rather than reported protocol revisions.

E4.justification: The 100-response error analysis, grader self-bias finding, and failure cases in Figures 8–12 are retained. Appendix E expands documentation of existing validation without introducing a distinct analysis; no context-length robustness experiment is added.

E5.justification: Both retain the stated 95% Wilson interval procedure, GPT-4o seed 22, grader correlation above 0.9, and error-annotation agreement of kappa 0.82. No additional repeated-run, uncertainty-reporting, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Added Table 2 results materially change the leading-model and human comparisons. GPT-5 reports pass@1 scores of 36.7%, 28.3%, and 19.5%, versus v4's best scores of 30.0%, 18.3%, and 10.5%; its dialogue score is numerically above the senior physician's 15.0%. Gemini 2.5-Pro reports 50.0% direct-diagnosis pass@5, versus the previous best 46.7%. Existing result rows remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D retains the same Wilson interval formula. The Two-Axis framework remains conceptual, with no added or revised formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, breadth–depth disconnect, reasoning-failure dominance, and human-performance-gap claims. Additional model results do not produce corresponding revisions to these core claims.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations invoking students' clinical training and metacognition versus VLM anchoring bias, identifies BERTScore as secondary, and explicitly excludes context-length robustness from scope. Most limitations in the new Section 6 already appeared in v4 Appendix A.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly explains section-prioritized note truncation, preservation of structured EHR fields, and absence of padding. Appendix E specifies three neurologists scoring 100 responses for existing grader validation. Appendix C adds checkpoint identifiers and decoding settings for the three new models; dataset-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds citations including MedSimSearch, Evo-PI, Lingshu, HuatuoGPT-Vision, and GMAI-MMBench, changes MultiMedQA's supporting reference, and removes the GPT-4o system-card reference. Other revisions concern bibliographic details of matched works. The breadth-versus-depth research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized revisions expand difficulty-level and grader explanations, introduce a main-text limitations section largely repeating Appendix A, add acknowledgments, and update affiliations and bibliography wording. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 5 gain three model rows, and Table 2 updates ranking emphasis. Existing figures are relocated or resized, including Figure 8 sharing a page with text in v5. All embedded figure graphics remain identical.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful model comparisons and clearer preprocessing and grader-validation documentation. However, Section 5.2 still calls MedGemma the top VLM despite GPT-5's higher scores, and the retained universal clinician-superiority claim conflicts with GPT-5's 19.5% versus the senior physician's 15.0% dialogue score. The new explanation asserting students' superior multi-turn performance and metacognition also lacks supporting comparative evidence. Broader evidence and better documentation coexist with poorer alignment between results and interpretation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
